findings.evidence: ExistsCompatible.lean:85 `@[expose] def restrict`; ExistsCompatible.lean:91-95 `restrict_apply` is the only characteristic lemma; SymplecticTransport.lean:69-71 `@[simp] lemma transport_toBilinForm ... := rfl`; StandardCompatible.lean:35 `public section` with no `@[expose]` on `stdSymplecticForm`. Nothing inside the file needs the exposed body: `restrict_apply` is proved in-file and every other use goes through it.
findings.fix: Drop `@[expose]` from `restrict` and add `@[simp] lemma restrict_toBilinForm (ω : SymplecticForm V) (L : Submodule ℝ V) (h : (ω.toBilinForm.restrict L).Nondegenerate) : (ω.restrict L h).toBilinForm = ω.toBilinForm.restrict L := (rfl)` next to `restrict_apply`.
findings.issue: `restrict` is the only `@[expose]` declaration in a file that otherwise uses a plain `public section`, and it lacks the `restrict_toBilinForm` restatement. Consumers who need `(ω.restrict L h).toBilinForm` — e.g. to iterate the splitting (symplectic reduction, the `Sym^g` local models the docstring names) or to apply any Mathlib `BilinForm` lemma to the restricted form — must unfold the body, which is exactly what the exposure is compensating for. Peer `SymplecticForm`-valued defs are unexposed and characterized by lemmas: `stdSymplecticForm` (StandardCompatible.lean:82, plain `public section`, only `stdSymplecticForm_apply`), `cotangentSymplecticForm` (Cotangent/Basic.lean:79), and `transport`, which carries both `transport_toBilinForm` and `transport_apply` (SymplecticTransport.lean:69-75).

findings.evidence: ExistsCompatible.lean:99-101 gives only `Disjoint → Nondegenerate`; the reverse exists in Mathlib only at the `BilinForm` layer (`Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/Orthogonal.lean:331` `restrict_nondegenerate_iff_isCompl_orthogonal`, and `:313` `isCompl_orthogonal_of_restrict_nondegenerate`), which requires the user to rewrite through `orthogonal_def` (Lagrangian/Basic.lean:66).
findings.fix: State the iff, `lemma restrict_nondegenerate_iff_disjoint_orthogonal (ω : SymplecticForm V) (L : Submodule ℝ V) : (ω.toBilinForm.restrict L).Nondegenerate ↔ Disjoint L (ω.orthogonal L)`, and derive the existing `nondegenerate_restrict_of_disjoint_orthogonal` as its `mpr`.
findings.issue: `restrict`'s defining hypothesis `(ω.toBilinForm.restrict L).Nondegenerate` is phrased in Mathlib's `BilinForm` vocabulary and is only characterized in one direction. Given `h : (ω.toBilinForm.restrict L).Nondegenerate`, the repo's own API offers no way back to `Disjoint L (ω.orthogonal L)` — the `SymplecticForm`-level condition that `isCompl_orthogonal_iff_disjoint` and `disjoint_orthogonal_orthogonal` consume — so a user handed a `ω.restrict L h` must drop to `LinearMap.BilinForm` to continue. The converse is unconditional (if `v ∈ L ⊓ ω.orthogonal L` then the restriction kills `v`), so no finite-dimensionality is needed.

findings.evidence: Uses of `apply_smul_add_smul_right`/`_left`: ExistsCompatible.lean:203, 205 (in `private lemma pairMap_injective`) and 245, 247 (in `disjoint_orthogonal_span_pair`); `exists_compatible_of_subsingleton`: line 294 only, inside `private theorem exists_compatible_aux`. The docstring's declaration list (lines 39-61) names `apply_smul_add_smul` but neither variant, and does not name `exists_compatible_of_subsingleton`.
findings.fix: Mark all three `private`; the file already marks the analogous helpers (`pairMap`, `planeEquiv`, `range_pairMap`, `isSymplectomorphism_planeEquiv`, `exists_compatible_restrict_span_pair`) private.
findings.issue: Three declarations are public but are used only by this file's own `private` helpers and `private theorem exists_compatible_aux`, and the module's own `## Main declarations` list omits all three: `apply_smul_add_smul_right` (line 114) and `apply_smul_add_smul_left` (line 120), one-line `simp [h]` consequences of the public `apply_smul_add_smul` with `ω x y = 1` baked in, and `exists_compatible_of_subsingleton` (line 278), the induction base subsumed by `exists_compatible` on any finite-dimensional space.

summary: The main existence theorems and the splitting lemmas are the right surface, but the new definition `SymplecticForm.restrict` exposes its body instead of carrying the `_toBilinForm` restatement its siblings have, its defining hypothesis is only characterized in one direction, and three helper lemmas that the module's own declaration list omits are left public.
